# §F — Controller tickets, boardctl-compatible workflows, and objective/assignment state
**Authority.** This is the single authority for ticket identity, registered workflow versions, objective/assignment mapping, expected-revision mutations, dependency readiness, durable transition events, board views, and ticket mutations. The machine contracts are in `contracts/section6-workflow.json`, `contracts/section6-transition-table.json`, `contracts/section6-state-mapping.json`, and the companion schemas. No other section or local board may define a competing edge.

## F.1 Controller boundary and one writer
A ticket is a durable, addressable work item. The controller ticket service is the sole authority for ticket identity, fields, graph edges, workflow state, authorization, compare-and-set, and transition events. It is reached through `chd_ticket_*` MCP tools or equivalent HTTP/CLI doors. Agents never edit a repository board or `/chd/*` key to mutate shared state.
The local boardctl-compatible JSONL board is a **derived mirror**. Export reads canonical records and includes `authority: controller`, source record, source revision, event references, and a derivation timestamp. An edit, commit, absent row, or worktree state cannot authorize a transition. Import is a CAS-checked reconciliation proposal by `ticket_id`; it reports added, updated, conflicts, and ignored rows, never deletes by absence, and never replaces a workflow binding.

## F.2 Registered workflows and migration
`WorkflowDefinition` is registered at `/chd/workflow/<workflow-id>/<version>` and immutable. Registration is `POST /v1/workflows`; read is `GET /v1/workflows/{id}/{version}`. A ticket pins one version. A change registers a new version and uses `POST /v1/workflows/{id}/{from}/migrations`. Migration records source/target versions, actor, reason, ticket ids, source expected revisions, and ordered migration/transition events. Validate all source revisions before the first write; write the migration event before a target-version transition; stop on a conflict and read back all committed events. See `examples/section6/migration-v1-v2.json`.
Every legal edge is declared with machine, from, to, actor, guard, input event, and error. A terminal state has no outgoing edge. For one machine/from/input event, guards are mutually exclusive; `validators/validate_section6.py` rejects contradictory tables. Workflow registration is centralized through `POST /v1/workflows`, and migration uses the immutable registration record rather than editing board rows.

## F.3 Request, CAS, and durable commit contract
Every mutation except create carries a JSON request with `request_id`, `expected_revision`, transition id, machine, from/to, actor and actor class, input event, reason, evidence refs, and canonical guard facts. Serialize with RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme over UTF-8; the dedupe digest is `sha256:c14n(request_body)`. The expected revision is an integer and part of the canonical bytes. Same request id plus same bytes replays the original result; changed bytes return `request_reuse_conflict`.
The controller performs, in order: authenticate/authorize; validate registered edge and exclusive guard; compare expected revision and request id; claim the request ledger; write the next record revision; write one transition event; write required links/audit; fsync the controller namespace; read back record and event; acknowledge. `revision_after = expected_revision + 1` and `revision_before = expected_revision`. Any failed validation or stale revision writes no business state. Errors include `ticket_revision_conflict`, `workflow_version_unknown`, `ticket_transition_not_allowed`, `transition_guard_conflict`, `dependency_not_satisfied`, `replacement_link_required`, `transition_event_missing`, and `durability_unverified`.
The event key is `/chd/ticket/<ticket-id>/event/m<seq:012d>`. Each event contains event id, ticket/objective/assignment ids, machine and transition id, from/to, actor/class, input event, guard, reason, evidence refs, expected and before/after revisions, request id, commit sequence, and writer. Event sequence and revisions are durable ordering facts; timestamps are metadata. A successful transition is not acknowledged without durable record, durable event, fsync, and readback. The event schema is `contracts/section6-event.schema.json`; every transition also has an audit denial/error result when authorization, guard, CAS, durability, or readback fails. If any companion write is uncertain, the request remains unknown until the journal/commit-marker recovery protocol in `tables/commit-protocol.csv` reconciles it; no response absence is treated as proof of no effect.

## F.4 State machines and complete mapping
The complete mapping is in `section6-state-mapping.json`. In summary:
| Layer | Owns | Success terminal | Non-success terminal | |---|---|---|---| | objective | director aggregate | `accepted` | `withdrawn`, `superseded`, `cancelled` | | assignment | director/assigned owner | `accepted` | `withdrawn`, `superseded`, `cancelled` | | ticket | controller projection of bound machine | `accepted` | `withdrawn`, `superseded`, `cancelled` | | send | send orchestrator | `closed` after verified outcome | `deferred`, `failed`, `cancelled` | | attempt | controller run coordinator | `verified` or proven `stopped` | `failed`, `cancelled`, `unknown` |
A report is correlated to exactly one send and current attempt. `report_submitted`, `report_blocked`, and `report_waiting_human` are mutually exclusive input events. A waiting report closes the attempt as waiting but leaves the logical send open; a successor attempt is explicit. A report, cancellation intent, timeout, or lease expiry is not stop proof.

## F.5 Legal acceptance exits
Stage policy has three independent booleans: composition required, delivery required, and approval required. After all required assignments are accepted and criteria evidence is present, the objective takes only the stages requested by its policy:
| Composition | Delivery | Approval | Legal path to `accepted` | |---|---|---|---| | no | no | no | assignments accepted → in-acceptance → accepted | | no | no | yes | assignments accepted → in-acceptance → approval resolved → accepted | | no | yes | no | assignments accepted → in-acceptance → delivering → delivery verified → accepted | | no | yes | yes | assignments accepted → in-acceptance → delivering → delivery verified → approval resolved → accepted | | yes | no | no | assignments accepted → in-acceptance → composing → composition accepted → accepted | | yes | no | yes | assignments accepted → in-acceptance → composing → composition accepted → approval resolved → accepted | | yes | yes | no | assignments accepted → in-acceptance → composing → composition accepted → delivering → delivery verified → accepted | | yes | yes | yes | assignments accepted → in-acceptance → composing → composition accepted → delivering → delivery verified → approval resolved → accepted |
An unrequested stage is never invented. Rejection records a reason and rework scope; it does not accept or erase the previous evidence. Withdrawal, supersession, and cancellation are terminal non-success outcomes. A superseding or replacement object must carry an explicit link.

## F.6 Dependencies and replacement
A dependency is satisfied only by an accepted producer with all required artifacts. `cancelled`, `withdrawn`, `superseded`, `failed`, `deferred`, and `unknown` never satisfy a dependency. A cancelled prerequisite sets each direct dependent to `blocked{prerequisite_cancelled}`. A replacement releases the dependent only after the replacement is accepted, supplies the required artifact, and the dependency edge durably records `replaces: <predecessor-id>` under director authority. Acceptance without the artifact remains blocked. A replacement without the link is refused with `replacement_link_required`.

## F.7 Boardctl mapping
| Boardctl concept | Canonical controller source | Rule | |---|---|---| | row id | `ticket_id` | stable, never reused | | title/kind/priority | TicketRecord | controller CAS update | | column | projected `state` | view only; never a write authority | | owner | `accountable_owner` | exactly one | | objective/assignment | linked ObjectiveRecord/AssignmentRecord | states remain separate | | dependency | graph edge + outcome/artifact | cancelled is not satisfied | | event | durable TicketEvent | one per successful transition | | import/export | controller API | reconciliation only; no delete-by-absence |
For keyset queries use `GET /v1/tickets?...&cursor=`. A successful export includes the source revision and authority marker. The board can be regenerated at any time; the controller record and event history are authoritative and cannot be rebuilt safely from a mirror.

## F.8 Required evidence
Validate schemas, `section6-transition-table.json`, migration example, optional-stage examples, and the derived mirror schema together with:
```bash python3 handbook/chd32/validators/validate_section6.py python3 -m json.tool handbook/chd32/contracts/section6-workflow.json >/dev/null python3 -m json.tool handbook/chd32/contracts/section6-transition-table.json >/dev/null ```
The validator must reject a duplicate edge, a terminal outgoing edge, a missing actor/guard/ input event/revision field, overlapping report guards, an unlinked replacement, or a cancelled prerequisite marked satisfied. It must accept all eight optional-stage combinations and the ordered migration example.
